fixes.explanation: Yes, baker, that's true. God says, "I answered you from the cloud of thunder…" (Psalm 81:7) Right before that, He says, "You called out in distress, and I rescued you…" His answer came with thunder, and I think that's one answer nobody had to ask Him to repeat.

Yes, baker. God says, "So I gave them up to their stubborn hearts to follow their own devices." (Psalm 81:12) Just before that, He says, "But My people would not listen to Me, and Israel would not obey Me." (Psalm 81:11) That's a serious line, and I think it's one to slow down for.
That's it, baker. Asaph says, "Sound the ram’s horn at the New Moon, and at the full moon on the day of our Feast." (Psalm 81:3) The horn goes with the calendar. Moon in the sky, horn in the air.

That sounds like a busy horn, friend. But Asaph ties it to the moon, not the sun: "Sound the ram’s horn at the New Moon, and at the full moon on the day of our Feast." (Psalm 81:3) Twice a day would wear out whoever's blowing it, and I'd know, because my mustache gets tired just from stamping.

You got it, baker. The psalm says God ordained it as a testimony for Joseph "…when he went out over the land of Egypt…" (Psalm 81:5) Egypt is the land the verse names. It's right there in the middle of the line.
Oh, friend, no. That's the opposite of what God says: "You called out in distress, and I rescued you…" (Psalm 81:7) They called, and He rescued them and answered them. Nobody got left on hold.

Parting waters is a big picture, friend, but that's not what the psalm says about Meribah. God says, "I tested you at the waters of Meribah." (Psalm 81:7) The word here is tested. That's the one thing this verse says happened there.

Nice try, friend, but no animal shows up in this verse. God says, "There must be no strange god among you, nor shall you bow to a foreign god." (Psalm 81:9) The warning here is about a strange god. That's the one thing He names.

That one's a stretch, friend, since the psalm never mentions Egypt here. God says, "So I gave them up to their stubborn hearts to follow their own devices." (Psalm 81:12) The verse before says, "But My people would not listen to Me, and Israel would not obey Me." (Psalm 81:11) So what He does is let them follow their own devices.

Reasonable guess, friend, but the psalm doesn't mention a prophet here. God says, "So I gave them up to their stubborn hearts to follow their own devices." (Psalm 81:12) Right before it, He says, "But My people would not listen to Me…" (Psalm 81:11) So He gave them up to follow their own devices.

That's a good thought, friend, but it's not in this verse. God says, "…how soon I would subdue their enemies and turn My hand against their foes!" (Psalm 81:14) He speaks of subduing enemies. That's the answer here.
